findings.evidence: Row claims version_status "published" with version "opt1-102". Per c2, "published" means the maintainer publishes a release identifier for this board and version copies it. SOURCE 1 (full protocol page excerpt) contains no release identifier: it states the benchmark title, authors, Opt@1 definition, scaffold note and dated changelog entries, but no release/version identifier, and the string "opt1-102" appears nowhere in SOURCE 1 or SOURCE 2. SOURCE 2 metadata carries only last_updated "2026-09-27" and total_tasks 102; a last_updated timestamp is an update stamp, not a release identifier, and changelog dates mark methodology changes, not named releases. The page therefore publishes no release identifier for this board, which per c2 is exactly the condition supporting version_status "snapshot"; claiming "published" is contradicted by the excerpt.
findings.repair: Set version_status to "snapshot" and version to the dated frozen identity (e.g., "snapshot-2026-11-04", this run's capture date); alternatively, keep "published" only if evidence of a maintainer-published release identifier that "opt1-102" copies is supplied.

uncertainties: I cannot recompute SHA-256 hashes or run transport/qualification checks; binding and integrity are the owner's executed responsibilities, not a defect in evidence.

Row notes cite the 2026-04-27 iteration-budget and 2026-07-12 network-isolation changelog entries but omit the 2026-09-27 changelog entry (improved elicitation asking models to keep measuring after their first speedup); this is an omission, not a contradiction, since the guard defines identity via total_tasks 102 and the Opt@1 setting, but the notes could be updated for completeness as current rows dated 2026-09-27 exist.
Description paraphrases 'a codebase' as 'a real codebase'; judged an acceptable restatement of SOURCE 1 text, not a mismatch.

One could argue metadata.last_updated is a published identifier; I judged it an update timestamp, and even under that reading version "opt1-102" copies no maintainer string, so the finding stands either way.
